quality_flags.notes: This image should be REJECTED at the quality gate before reaching the VLM. The opencv-python pre-processing step (Laplacian variance blur detection) should catch this and return ALL checks as UNCERTAIN without making an expensive VLM API call. This is the correct system behavior.

training_notes.expected_system_behavior: QUALITY GATE REJECTION — the image pre-processor should detect blur score 0.04 and short-circuit the pipeline, setting all check verdicts to UNCERTAIN without calling the Gemini API.
training_notes.verdict_policy: NEVER GUESS. When image quality is insufficient, ALL checks must return UNCERTAIN. Returning PASS or FAIL when evidence is unreadable is a worse outcome than UNCERTAIN — it produces false confidence.
prd_rules_triggered: PRD §8.1 — The system must not report PASS or FAIL for any check that cannot be verified from the available image evidence.
TRD §3.3 — Image quality gating must run BEFORE VLM inference. Blur detection (Laplacian variance < 0.40) must trigger UNCERTAIN for all checks.
training_notes.pipeline_impact: This scenario validates the opencv quality gate, NOT the VLM. The correct outcome proves the quality gate is working — not that the VLM can somehow read blurry images.
training_notes.vrd_model_learning_value: CRITICAL — This is the only image in the dataset that should short-circuit the entire VLM pipeline. It validates the quality gating layer, confirms the UNCERTAIN verdict policy under poor conditions, and ensures the model never hallucinates evidence from unreadable images.
training_notes.contrast_with: scenario_01 (perfect quality, all PASS) — the maximum quality contrast pair in the dataset
